clue.text: Article put on aircraft carrying journo from E London

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it, as a plane carries cargo

parts.note: a bomber jet is a military aircraft
a journalist is a hack, and a Cockney from the East End drops the H, giving 'ack

explanation.surface: A newspaper reporter from London's East End is stowed on a plane, with something attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aircraft' is two words' worth, BOMBER JET, and 'carrying' puts ACK between them. Cockneys (East Londoners) traditionally drop their aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment is something you put on, and this zipped flying jacket is one such item of clothing.

clue.text: Concession to the elderly that's enough to be getting on with?

definitions.text: Concession to the elderly that's enough to be getting on with?

parts.words: Concession to the elderly that's enough to be getting on with?
parts.note: a free travel permit for older people; showing it is enough to let you get on board, with a pun on 'getting on' meaning ageing

explanation.surface: A modest allowance for pensioners that will do for the time being.
explanation.definitionFit: Older people in Britain get free local bus travel by showing a permit, a concession they can board with.

clue.text: Food processing areas come without specialist?

indicators.note: without means outside, so the rearranged letters go around the other piece
processing works the letters over, so they are rearranged

parts.note: niche as an adjective means specialised, catering to a narrow market

explanation.surface: Kitchen areas run by food processors manage without an expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processing' rearranges AREAS COME into MACAROESE, and 'without' (outside) puts that around NICHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta baked in a cheese sauce is a familiar dish, so it is an example of food.

clue.text: Praise no longer key

parts.note: ex- describes a former partner or holder, one who is no longer so
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Applause is no longer the crucial thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To glorify or extol someone is to praise them highly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Spot fine, then jail for West Indian

parts.note: a spot of trouble, a tight spot, is a jam
A1 means first-rate or fine, here written AI
the can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Caught out, someone is fined and then locked up, said to be from the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaica is a Caribbean island in the West Indies, so a native of it is a West Indian.

clue.text: 99, maybe, or two more?

definitions.meaning: a 99 is a British ice cream with a chocolate flake, served in a wafer holder
two more than 99 is 101, which reads as C (Roman 100) followed by ONE

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a number: ninety-nine, or perhaps a couple higher?
explanation.walkthrough: A 99 is a soft ice cream in a wafer cone with a chocolate flake, sold from British ice-cream vans. 101 written half in Roman numerals and half in words gives C plus ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The 99 ice cream comes in a wafer holder, which is the example the clue hints at.

clue.text: On reflection, short feature appeared wasted

indicators.note: a mirror reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run backwards
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a detail is a feature or particular
came, as in turned up, means appeared

explanation.surface: Thinking back, a brief characteristic seemed to be a waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of the feature word; 'On reflection' then turns the whole run DETAICAME round, so the reversal covers both pieces, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wasted away is gaunt and extremely thin, the sense the answer carries.

clue.text: Corrupt practice of daughter in marring energy recycling

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the rearranged letters
recycling reprocesses material into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A daughter's dishonest habit of spoiling energy-saving recycling schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycling' rearranges MARRING ENERGY; 'in' puts D among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigging electoral boundaries for party advantage is a notoriously corrupt political practice.

clue.text: Girl who'd come out with gentleman heading north remains

parts.note: a debutante, or deb, was a young woman formally 'coming out' into society

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: Sir is the title or address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A society girl's debut, with a gentleman heading off northwards, is all that is left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' in a down light reverses SIR to RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Scattered rubble and fragments left after destruction are the remains of something.

clue.text: Bones found in bag next to top drawer?

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch in an animal or plant
a drawer is an artist; a top one is a Royal Academician, RA

explanation.surface: Skeleton remains turn up in a holdall beside the uppermost drawer of a chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' is one who draws: an RA is a member of the Royal Academy of Arts, a top British artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of sacrum, the triangular bones at the base of the spine.

clue.text: An element of comic book language?

definitions.meaning: manga are Japanese comic books, and -ese makes a jargon or language, as in journalese

explanation.surface: A question about one ingredient of the way comics talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is split as MANGA plus -NESE, a mock jargon modelled on Japanese.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a grey transition metal on the periodic table, a chemical element.

clue.text: Where one takes off, but doesn't actually undress?

definitions.meaning: aircraft take off from a runway or landing field
a pretend striptease, like playing air guitar, is a strip in the air

explanation.surface: A place to remove one's clothes, but without truly getting undressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple runway for light aircraft is the place a flight lifts off.

clue.text: Glass raised to oneself daily?

definitions.meaning: a looking glass is held up in front of one's own face

explanation.surface: A drinking glass lifted in a toast to yourself every day.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Mirror is a national British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A looking glass is what you hold up to see your own reflection.

clue.text: Belt for strangling with is a hazard of course

indicators.note: strangling wraps tightly around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a strap is a belt
and means together with

explanation.surface: A belt used to throttle someone is a dangerous thing, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally' but means 'on a golf course'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunker on a golf course, chiefly American usage, is one of its hazards.

clue.text: Petty in the extreme? That is the way with adolescents

indicators.note: with attaches the adolescents to the other pieces, here at the front

parts.note: teenagers are teens
i.e. abbreviates id est, meaning that is
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Adolescents are notably small-minded: that's how they are.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of teensy, very small, so smallest of all: petty to the utmost degree.

clue.text: Lord's conclusion perhaps is baffling

definitions.meaning: at cricket grounds such as Lord's, the close of a day's play is called this

explanation.surface: The way a nobleman's argument ends is perplexing.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground, not a peer; the term marks the end of a day's play, when the wickets are pulled up.
explanation.definitionFit: The close of play in cricket is named after the wicket posts drawn at the end.

clue.text: Work on hand satisfied patient of mine?

definitions.meaning: beauty treatment of the nails and hands
a person I heal, who would be a satisfied patient

explanation.surface: A job in progress pleased a doctor's patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Trimming and polishing fingernails is cosmetic work done on the hand.

clue.text: Female motorists requiring assistance briefly

parts.note: the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: help is assistance

explanation.surface: Women drivers whose cars break down call for quick help.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is a British breakdown service for motorists.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's given name, so it stands for a female in crosswords.

clue.text: Artist's career's having to be pigeon-holed

indicators.note: pigeon-holed means slotted into a compartment, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to career is to run headlong, so a career's a runs

explanation.surface: A painter's working life has to be put into a neat category.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist's' reads as 'Artist is', so the 's is a link; 'career' is the verb meaning to rush, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flemish Baroque painter is a famous old master, a painter by name.

clue.text: In place of patient article, engineer moves anticipating conflict?

parts.note: a hospital ward is where a patient stays
an is the indefinite article
CE is a civil engineer

explanation.surface: In a hospital, an engineer shifts things expecting a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual dance performed before battle is a series of moves made ahead of fighting.

clue.text: Condition, but not necessarily range, of person under discussion?

definitions.text: Condition, but not necessarily range, of person under discussion?

parts.words: Condition, but not necessarily range, of person under discussion?
parts.note: someone being talked about is said to have burning ears; the whole word also means hearing range

explanation.surface: Asking what state, if not what distance, the subject of a debate is in.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the distance within which a voice can be heard: hearing range.

clue.text: Point after brother, making face

indicators.note: after places the point behind the brother

parts.note: east is a compass point

explanation.surface: Following a sibling, a point gets made.
explanation.definitionFit: To breast a wave or a hill is to face and meet it head on, a verb sense.

clue.text: Tragedy of family left packing possessions

parts.note: kin are family
gear is belongings

explanation.surface: A family's sad departure, leaving with their belongings packed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play about an old king and his daughters is one of his tragedies.

clue.text: Set to consume game, finding something less appetising

indicators.note: consuming takes the other piece inside, swallowing it

parts.note: to gel is to set, as a jelly does
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Ready to eat game but finding a less tempting meal.
explanation.walkthrough: RU, rugby union, is a common crossword game.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin oatmeal porridge is notoriously unappealing fare, as in Oliver Twist.

clue.text: Bundle of cash one found in dry river bed

parts.note: a wad is a roll of banknotes
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A roll of money is discovered in a dried-up watercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arabic-speaking deserts this is a valley that holds water only in the rainy season.

clue.text: Old film about a ref, songs from the right shows

indicators.note: reading from the right means the letters are taken backwards
the letters show within the run of words, spanning their boundaries

explanation.surface: An old film about a referee, with songs, is screened from the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' finds UTAREFSON in 'about a ref, songs'; 'from the right' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Murnau's 1922 silent vampire picture is a classic of early cinema.

clue.text: Bathsheba's husband's backpedalling a shock perhaps for all

indicators.note: backpedalling goes in reverse, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all

explanation.surface: A Biblical husband retreats from a shock that may suit everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husband's' is 'husband is'. U is the British film rating meaning suitable for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament, David had this Hittite soldier killed to marry his wife.

clue.text: My small three wheeler: get off!

parts.note: a trike is a tricycle
to alight is to get off a vehicle

explanation.surface: An owner tells someone to climb off a little tricycle.
explanation.definitionFit: An old British exclamation of surprise, like 'Goodness!' or 'My!'
